match.reason: Neither bank point teaches young people acting personally or in their communities to advocate for better and fairer health; they cover linked youth health issues and the community health resources and barriers to using them.

draft.title: Youth advocacy
card: Advocacy is speaking up for a cause or for other people. In health, it aims to bring about better and fairer health for a person or a group.
things a young person does in their own life, such as learning about an issue, making healthy choices or speaking up for themselves.
things done with or for others, such as joining a youth council, running a school awareness campaign or writing to a local member of parliament.
Both kinds of action can help. Young people know what their peers face, so their voices can show decision makers what needs to change.
draft.remember: Advocacy is speaking up for better and fairer health, in your own life and in your community.

a.q: Which action is an example of youth advocacy for health?
opts: Starting a petition for a skate park at a local youth centre
Reading a news story about a new health program
Waiting for the council to decide where to build a park
Taking part in a survey that a school gives to every student
a.why: A petition is a way of speaking up for better health, because active play supports wellbeing. The other options are about reading, waiting or answering, so they do not involve speaking up for a cause.
a.clue: Which one means speaking up rather than only taking part?

b.q: Priya, 16, tells her friends about the health risks of vaping and asks her school to hold a student-led talk on it. What kind of action is the request to the school?
opts: Community action, because it speaks up for a group
Personal action, because Priya made the request herself
Not advocacy, because it is only about one health issue
Not advocacy, because Priya is not an adult
b.why: The request asks the school to act for all students, so it is community action. Personal action is about a person's own life. It is tempting to choose personal, because Priya acted herself, but what matters is who the action is for.
b.clue: Think about who the request is meant to help.

a.best: Starting a petition for a skate park at a local youth centre
also_right: Reading a news story about a new health program

b.best: Community action, because it speaks up for a group

proposal.title: Youth advocacy
card: Advocacy is speaking up for a cause or for other people. In health, it aims to bring about better and fairer health for a person or a group.
Advocacy means raising your voice so others hear. Reading about an issue or making a quiet healthy choice can be a good start, but it is not advocacy on its own.
speaking up in your own life for your own health, such as asking a doctor questions or saying no to peer pressure.
speaking up with or for others, such as joining a youth council, running a school awareness campaign or writing to a local member of parliament.
proposal.remember: Advocacy is speaking up so others hear, for your own health or for your community's.

a.q: Which action is an example of youth advocacy for health?
opts: Starting a petition for safer bike paths near the school
Reading a news story about a new youth health program
Quietly choosing water instead of soft drink at lunch
Waiting for the council to decide on new bike paths
a.why: A petition speaks up to decision makers for better and fairer health, so it is advocacy. Choosing water is a healthy choice, but it is made quietly and no one is asked to change anything, so it is not advocacy on its own.
a.clue: Which one makes someone else hear a call for change?
